hints: Notice the stone is pulled by two $T$ forces at an angle, with $6 \text{ cm}$ shown as the horizontal distance and $10 \text{ cm}$ as the length of each side.
Only the components pointing forward toward the $6 \text{ cm}$ direction add together - the up and down components from the $16 \text{ cm}$ total height cancel by symmetry.
Find $\cos\theta$ from the triangle with hypotenuse $10 \text{ cm}$ and adjacent side $6 \text{ cm}$, then add $2T\cos\theta$.
walkthrough: Identify the forces on the stone: two tension forces each of magnitude $T$, one along the upper cord and one along the lower cord.
By symmetry about the horizontal dashed line, the upward component of the top $T$ cancels the downward component of the bottom $T$. The resultant is purely horizontal.
For each side, the horizontal component is $T\cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the cord and the horizontal.

From the diagram, each side forms a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $10 \text{ cm}$ and horizontal adjacent side $6 \text{ cm}$, so $\cos\theta = 6/10 = 3/5$. The vertical half-side is $8 \text{ cm}$, consistent with $6$-$8$-$10$.
One horizontal component is $T \times 6/10 = 3T/5$. Two sides give $2 \times 3T/5 = 6T/5$.

options.A: This is only one horizontal component $T \times 6/10$. The stone is pulled by two sides of the cord, so the total is twice this.
options.B: The two horizontal components add to $2T \times 6/10 = 6T/5$ while the equal vertical components cancel.
options.C: This uses the $8 \text{ cm}$ vertical side $2T \times 8/10$. The vertical components act in opposite directions and cancel, not add.
options.D: This adds the magnitudes $T+T$ directly and ignores that the two $T$ forces are at an angle, so only their forward components add.
